name: Lutetium
occurrence: The rarest and most expensive naturally-occurring lanthanide to isolate, found in trace amounts in monazite ore.
majorUses: PET scan detector crystals (lutetium oxyorthosilicate scintillators)
notableCharacteristics: Sits at the very end of the lanthanide series and, with a full 4f¹⁴ subshell, is sometimes debated as technically belonging to the d-block rather than the f-block.
ncertRelevance: boundary/classification debate at end of lanthanide series
whyHere: With its 4f subshell already completely filled and its one extra electron going into 5d, lutetium sits right at the boundary between the f-block and d-block, which is exactly why some periodic tables classify it as the first element of the third transition series instead.
didYouKnow: Lutetium-177 is used in a targeted radiotherapy approach for certain cancers, where it's attached to a molecule that seeks out tumour cells specifically, delivering radiation with much less damage to surrounding healthy tissue.
genZNote: Technically might not even belong in the lanthanide series depending who you ask. The block boundary's biggest argument starter.
